questions.q: Which one of the following Five Year Plans recognised human development as the core of all development efforts? [1995]
questions.e: In the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-1997), the top priority was given to the development of human resources, which included employment, education, and public health as the core of all development efforts.

questions.q: Which of the following are among the non-plan expenditures of the Government of India? 1️⃣ Defence expenditure 2️⃣ Subsidies 3️⃣ All expenditures linked with the previous plan periods 4️⃣ Interest payment [1995, 1997]
questions.e: Non-plan expenditures include non-developmental expenditures such as interest payments, subsidies, defence expenditure, and civil administration. It also includes developmental expenditure and expenditure on projects left unfinished from previous plan periods.

questions.q: What is the annual rate aimed in the Eighth Five Year Plan? [1995]
questions.e: The targeted annual growth rate for the Eighth Five Year Plan was set at 5.6%, although the actual growth rate achieved was 6.7%.

questions.q: The largest source of financing the public sector outlay of the Eighth Five Year Plan comes from: [1995]
questions.e: According to the financing table for the Eighth Plan, capital receipts (which include government borrowings) accounted for 63.1% of domestic resources, making it the largest source.

questions.q: The New Exim Policy announced in 1992, is for period of: [1995]
questions.e: The New Exim Policy was announced for a five-year period, specifically from April 1, 1992, to March 31, 1997.

questions.q: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): An important policy instrument of economic liberalization is reduction in import duties on capital goods. Reason (R): Reduction in import duties would help the local entrepreneurs to improve technology to face the global markets. [1996]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true R is not a correct explanation
questions.e: Both statements are correct; reducing import duties on capital goods is a key tool for liberalization as it allows domestic industries to acquire better technology at lower costs to compete globally.

questions.q: The Eighth Five Year Plan is different from the earliest ones. The critical difference lies in the fact that: [1996]
o: considerable emphasis is placed on infrastructure growth
it has a major thrust on agricultural and rural development
it has a considerably larger outlay compared to the earlier plans
questions.e: The Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) had a significantly larger outlay than previous plans, with a specific heavy emphasis on the energy sector to achieve its growth targets.

questions.q: Technical assistance Programme in India on intergovernmental bilateral agreements, mainly provide: [1996]
o: Soft loans which are required to be paid back with interest
Food assistance to be paid back
Grants, not required to be paid back
questions.e: Technical assistance involves aid using highly educated or trained personnel. In the context of the provided solutions, grants are usually provided through international aid agencies and are not required to be paid back.

questions.q: Consider the following items imported by India: 1️⃣ Capital goods 2️⃣ Petroleum 3️⃣ Pearls and precious stones 4️⃣ Chemicals 5️⃣ Iron and Steel. The correct sequence of the decreasing order of these items (as per 94-95 figures), in terms of value is: [1996]
questions.e: Based on 1994-95 figures, the value of imports in decreasing order was led by Petroleum, followed by Capital goods, then Pearls/Precious stones, Chemicals, and Iron and Steel.

questions.q: The Sixth and the Eighth Five Year Plans covered the period 1980-1985 and 1992-1997 respectively. The Seventh Five Year Plan covered the period: [1997]
questions.e: The Seventh Five Year Plan ran from 1985 to 1990. The period between 1990 and 1992 was considered a "plan holiday" before the Eighth Plan commenced.

questions.q: Economic Survey in India is published officially, every year by the: [1998]
o: Ministry of Industries, Govt. of India
Ministry of Finance, Govt. of India
questions.e: The Economic Survey of India is an annual document released by the Ministry of Finance. It is typically presented in Parliament just before the Union Budget to review the economy's performance.

questions.q: Which one of the following regions of the world supplies the maximum of our imported commodities (in terms of rupee value)? [1998]
questions.e: According to the 1998 data provided in the text, Asia and Oceania was the region that supplied the maximum value of imported commodities to India.

questions.q: The planning process in the industries sector in India has assumed a relatively less important position in the nineties as compared to that in the earlier period. Which one of the following is not true in this regard? [1999]
o: The focus of planning has shifted to sectors like human resource
With the advent of liberalisation, industrial investment development have largely been placed within the domain of private and multinational sectors
The nation's priorities have shifted away from industrial development to rural development
With market assuming a central place, the role of central planning in many sectors has been rendered redundant
questions.e: Statements a, b, and c correctly reflect the changes post-liberalization where the market and private sector took a lead role. However, it is not true that priorities shifted entirely away from industry to rural development; rather, the method of industrial growth changed.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the objective of National Renewal Fund? [1999]
o: For human resource development such as full literacy, employment population control, housing and drinking water
For the development of infrastructure such as energy, transport communications and irrigation
To safeguard the interests of workers who may be affected by technological upgradation of industry or closure of sick units
To develop the core sector of the economy
questions.e: The National Renewal Fund (NRF) was established in 1992 following the New Industrial Policy of 1991 to provide a safety net for workers affected by industrial restructuring or the closure of sick units.

questions.q: The Employment Assurance Scheme envisages financial assistance to rural areas for guaranteeing employment to at least: [1999]
o: 50 percent of the men seeking jobs in rural areas
one person in a rural landless household living below the poverty line
50 percent of the men and women seeking jobs in rural areas
one man and one woman in a rural family living below the poverty line
questions.e: Launched in 1993, the Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) was designed to provide gainful employment during lean agricultural seasons to a maximum of two adults per family in rural areas.

questions.q: A rise in 'SENSEX' means: [2000]
o: a rise in prices of shares of all companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange
a rise in prices of shares of all companies belonging to a group of companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange
an overall rise in prices of shares of group of companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange
a rise in prices of shares of all companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange
questions.e: A rise in the SENSEX indicates an overall positive trend in the share prices of the representative group of companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange, reflecting investor confidence in the economy.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The rate of growth of India's exports has shown an appreciable increase after 1991. Reason (R): The Govt. of India has resorted to devaluation. [2000]
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Post-1991, India devalued the rupee, making Indian goods cheaper for foreign buyers. This directly contributed to the increase in the growth rate of exports.

questions.q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer: 1️⃣ A. UN Development Programme - 4. Human Development Report 2️⃣ B. National Council of Applied Economic Research - 1. India Development Report 3️⃣ C. Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research - 2. India Development Report 4️⃣ D. World Bank - 3. World Development Report [2000]
questions.e: The UNDP publishes the Human Development Report. The NCAER is associated with the India Human Development Report (referred to in hints as B-1). The IGIDR publishes the India Development Report, and the World Bank publishes the World Development Report.

questions.q: "...instil into the vast millions of workers, men and women, who actually do the job, a sense of partnership and of cooperative performance..." The above passage relates to: [2000]
questions.e: Community Development is a process that seeks to empower individuals and groups by providing them with skills to effect change and foster a sense of collective partnership in solving common problems.

questions.q: Economic liberalisation in India started with: [2000]
o: doing away with procedural formalities for foreign direct investment
substantial changes in industrial licensing policy
questions.e: The liberalization process in India is widely considered to have begun with major changes to the industrial licensing policy, effectively ending the "License Raj" for most sectors.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: The Indian rupee is fully convertible: 1️⃣ in respect of Current Account of Balance of payment 2️⃣ in respect of Capital Account of Balance of payment 3️⃣ into gold [2000]
questions.e: Since the 1991 reforms, the Indian rupee has been made fully convertible on the Current Account, but it remains only partially convertible on the Capital Account.

questions.q: The growth rate of per capita income at current prices is higher than that of per capita income at constant prices, because the latter takes into account the rate of: [2000]
questions.e: Constant price calculations adjust for inflation (increase in price level). Because current prices include the effects of inflation, the growth rate appears higher than when measured at constant prices.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1️⃣ Market borrowing 2️⃣ Treasury bills 3️⃣ Special securities issued to RBI. Which of these is/are components(s) of internal debt? [2001]
questions.e: Internal debt refers to the portion of total government debt owed to lenders within the country. This includes market borrowings, Treasury bills, and special securities issued to the RBI.

questions.q: Global capital flows to developing countries increased significantly during the nineties. In view of the East Asian financial crisis and Latin American experience, which type of inflow is good for the host country? [2002]
questions.e: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is considered more stable and beneficial because it is long-term, non-debt creating, and involves physical assets or management control, making it harder to withdraw quickly compared to portfolio investment.

questions.q: Five Year Plan in India is finally approved by: [2002]
o: President on the advice of Prime Minister
questions.e: While the Planning Commission formulated the Five Year Plans, the final authority for approval was the National Development Council (NDC), which included Chief Ministers of all states and was headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: A country is said to be a debt trap if: [2002]
o: it has to abide by the conditionalities imposed by the International Monetary fund.
the World Bank charges a very high rate of interest on outstanding as well as new loans
it has been refused loans or aid by creditors abroad
it has to borrow to make interest payments on outstanding loans
questions.e: A debt trap is a financial situation where a borrower is forced to take on new debt just to pay the interest on existing debts, leading to a cycle of increasing indebtedness.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct statement? Service tax is a/an: [2006]
o: indirect tax levied by the Central Government.
direct tax levied by the Central Government.
indirect tax levied by the State Government.
direct tax levied by the State Government.
questions.e: Service tax (prior to GST) was an indirect tax levied by the Central Government. Indirect taxes are those where the liability to pay can be shifted from the initial taxpayer to another person (the consumer).

questions.q: During which Five Year Plan was the Emergency clamped, new elections took place and the Janata Party was elected? [2009]
questions.e: These political events occurred during the period of the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1978). The plan was terminated a year early by the new Janata Party government.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Indian Planning: 1️⃣ The Second Five-Year Plan emphasized on the establishment of heavy industries. 2️⃣ The Third Five-Year Plan introduced the concept of import substitution as a strategy for industrialization. [2009]
questions.e: The Second Five-Year Plan focused on rapid industrialization and heavy industries. The Third Plan focused on agriculture and self-sufficiency in food grains; while import substitution was part of the era, the primary focus of the Third Plan was different.

questions.q: Which one of the following brings out the publication called "Energy Statistics" from time to time? [2009]
questions.e: The publication "Energy Statistics" is released by the Central Statistical Organization (CSO), which falls under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

questions.q: In the context of independent India's economy, which one of the following was the earliest event to take place? [2009]
o: Nationalization of State Bank of India
questions.e: The Banking Regulation Act was enacted in 1949. The First Five-Year Plan started in 1951, SBI was nationalized in 1955, and Life Insurance was nationalized in 1956.

questions.q: The SEZ Act, 2005 which came into effect in February 2006 has certain objectives. In this context, consider the following: 1️⃣ Development of infrastructure facilities. 2️⃣ Promotion of investment from foreign sources. 3️⃣ Promotion of exports of services only. [2010]
questions.e: The SEZ Act aims to promote the export of both goods and services, not "services only." Its primary goals are creating infrastructure and attracting both domestic and foreign investment for export-led growth.

questions.q: A great deal of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) to India comes from Mauritius than from many major and mature economies like UK and France. Why? [2010]
o: India has double taxation avoidance agreement with Mauritius
Impending dangers of global climatic change prompt Mauritius to make huge investments in India
India has preference for certain countries as regards receiving FDI
Most citizens of Mauritius have ethnic identity with India and so they feel secure to invest in India
questions.e: India's Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) with Mauritius allowed investors to route funds through Mauritius to take advantage of lower tax rates, a practice known as treaty shopping.

questions.q: In the context of the India-based Neutrino Observatory, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Neutrinos are chargeless elementary particles that travel close to the speed of light. 2️⃣ Neutrinos are created in nuclear reactions of beta decay. 3️⃣ Neutrinos have a negligible, but non-zero mass. 4️⃣ Trillions of Neutrinos pass through human body every second. [2010]
questions.e: Neutrinos are fundamental particles that are electrically neutral, travel at nearly the speed of light, and have a very tiny mass. They are produced in various nuclear reactions and pass through matter, including humans, with minimal interaction.

questions.q: Inclusive growth as enunciated in the Eleventh Five Year Plan does not include one of the following: [2010]
questions.e: Inclusive growth refers to "shared" or "pro-poor" growth that ensures benefits reach all sections of society. Strengthening capital markets is a function of the financial sector and is not a direct component of the inclusive growth framework.

questions.q: Who of the following shall cause every recommendation made by the Finance Commission to be laid before each House of Parliament? [2010]
questions.e: Under Article 281 of the Constitution, the President is responsible for laying the Finance Commission's recommendations, along with an explanatory memorandum, before both Houses of Parliament.

questions.q: Which one of the following is responsible for the preparation and presentation of Union Budget to the Parliament? [2010]
questions.e: The Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) within the Ministry of Finance is the nodal agency responsible for preparing and presenting the Union Budget.

questions.q: Consider the following actions by the Government: 1️⃣ Cutting the tax rates 2️⃣ Increasing the government spending 3️⃣ Abolishing the subsidies. Which of the above actions can be considered a part of the "fiscal stimulus" package? [2010]
questions.e: A fiscal stimulus is intended to boost economic activity. Cutting taxes leaves more money with consumers/businesses, and increasing government spending directly creates demand. Abolishing subsidies would likely reduce spending and increase prices, which is the opposite of a stimulus.

questions.q: In the context of India's Five Year Plans, a shift in the pattern of industrialization, with lower emphasis on heavy industries and more on infrastructure begins in: [2010]
questions.e: While infrastructure was always present, a distinct shift toward infrastructure development as a primary focus over heavy industry began specifically during the Sixth Plan and was further emphasized in the Eighth Plan.

questions.q: With reference to the National Investment Fund, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The assets in the National Investment Fund are managed by the Union Ministry of Finance. 2️⃣ The National Investment Fund is to be maintained within the Consolidated Fund of India. 3️⃣ Certain Asset Management companies are appointed as the fund managers. 4️⃣ A certain proportion of annual income is used for financing select social sectors. [2010]
questions.e: The NIF is managed by professional fund managers (Asset Management Companies), not the Ministry. It is kept outside the Consolidated Fund of India, and 75% of its income is used for social sectors like health and education.

questions.q: In India, the tax proceeds of which one of the following as a percentage of gross tax revenue has significantly declined in the last five years? [2010]
questions.e: Between 1992 and 2007, the share of Excise duty in total tax revenue dropped from 41.3% to 25.1% due to tax restructuring and the growth of other tax components like service tax.

questions.q: Which one of the following authorities makes recommendation to the Governor of a State as to the principles for determining the taxes and duties which may be appropriated by the Panchayats in that particular State? [2010]
o: Panchayati Raj Ministry of that State
questions.e: The State Finance Commission is constitutionally mandated to recommend principles for the distribution of tax proceeds between the State and Panchayats, as well as the types of taxes Panchayats can levy.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In India, taxes on transactions in Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets are levied by the Union. 2️⃣ In India, taxes on transactions in Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets are collected by the States. [2010]
questions.e: Taxes on transactions in stock exchanges and futures markets are both levied and collected by the Union Government.

questions.q: India has experienced persistent and high food inflation in the recent past. What could be the reasons? 1️⃣ Due to a gradual switchover to the cultivation of commercial crops, the area under the cultivation of food grains has steadily decreased in the last five years by about 30%. 2️⃣ As a consequence of increasing incomes, the consumption patterns of the people have undergone a significant change. 3️⃣ The food supply chain has structural constraints. [2011-I]
questions.e: High food inflation is driven by shifting consumption patterns toward protein-rich foods as incomes rise, and by structural inefficiencies in the supply chain. The claim of a 30% decrease in food grain area is factually incorrect.

questions.q: In terms of economy, the visit by foreign nationals to witness the XIX commonwealth games in India amounted to: [2011-I]
questions.e: Spending by foreign tourists within a country is considered an "invisible export" because it results in the inflow of foreign exchange into the domestic economy.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements appropriately describes the "fiscal stimulus"? [2011-I]
o: It is government's intensive action on financial institutions to ensure disbursement of loans to agriculture and allied sectors to promote greater food production and contain food inflation.
It is an intense affirmative action of the government to boost economic activity in the country.
It is a massive investment by the government in manufacturing sector to ensure the supply of goods to meet the demand surge caused by rapid economic growth.
It is an extreme affirmative action by the government to pursue its policy of financial inclusion.
questions.e: A fiscal stimulus is a set of government policies (spending increases or tax cuts) used to boost economic activity, particularly during periods of slowdown.

questions.q: Consider the following actions which the government can take: 1️⃣ Devaluing the domestic currency. 2️⃣ Reduction in the export subsidy. 3️⃣ Adopting suitable policies which attract greater FDI and more funds from FIIs. Which of the above action/actions can help in reducing the current account deficit? [2011-I]
questions.e: Devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports costlier, helping reduce the trade deficit. Attracting FDI/FII provides the necessary capital to finance or offset the deficit, although the primary tool for the deficit itself is trade-related.

questions.q: Both Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) are related to investment in a country. Which one of the following statements best represents an important difference between the two? [2011-I]
o: FII helps bring better management skills and technology, while FDI only brings in capital.
FDI flows only into the secondary market while FII targets primary market
FII is considered to be more stable than FDI.
FII helps in increasing capital availability in general, while FDI only targets specific sectors.
questions.e: FDI is targeted at specific enterprises and often brings technology and management. FII is portfolio investment in the secondary market, which increases overall capital availability but can be more volatile than FDI.

questions.q: With reference to "Aam Admi Bima Yojana", consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The member insured under the scheme must be the head of the family or an earning member of the family in a rural landless house-hold. 2️⃣ The member insured must be in the age group of 30 to 65 years. 3️⃣ There is a provision for free scholarship for up to two children of the insured who are studying between classes 9 and 12. [2011-I]
questions.e: The age group for the Aam Admi Bima Yojana is 18 to 59 years, not 30 to 65. The scheme covers rural landless households and provides educational scholarships for children in grades 9-12.

questions.q: Microfinance is the provision of financial services to people of low-income groups. This includes both the consumers and the self-employed. The service/services rendered under microfinance is/are: 1️⃣ Savings facilities 2️⃣ Fund Transfer facilities 3️⃣ Credit facilities 4️⃣ Insurance facilities [2011-I]
questions.e: Microfinance is a broad movement aimed at providing low-income households with a full range of high-quality financial services, including credit, savings, insurance, and money transfers.

questions.q: Among the following who are eligible to benefit from the "Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act"? [2011-I]
o: Adult members of households of all backward communities
Adult members of below poverty line (BPL) households
Adult members of only the scheduled caste and scheduled tribe households
questions.e: MGNREGA is a universal program in rural areas; any adult member of a rural household who is willing to do unskilled manual work is eligible to apply.

questions.q: With reference to the Finance Commission of India, which of the following statements is correct? [2011-I]
o: None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct in his context
It encourages the inflow of foreign capital for infrastructure development
It facilitates the proper distribution of finances among the Public Sector Undertakings
It ensures transparency in financial administration
questions.e: The Finance Commission's primary constitutional role is to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and States and to determine principles for grants-in-aid to states.

questions.q: What is the difference between "vote-on-account" and "interim budget"? 1️⃣ The provision of a "vote-on-account" is used by a regular Government, while an "interim budget" is a provision used by a caretaker Government 2️⃣ A "vote-on-account" only deals with the expenditure in Government budget, while an "interim budget" includes both expenditure and receipts [2011-I]
questions.e: A vote-on-account is specifically for the expenditure side to keep the government running for a short period. An interim budget is a full budget including receipts, typically presented in an election year. Caretaker governments do not usually present budgets.

questions.q: Why is the offering of "teaser loans" by commercial banks a cause of economic concern? 1️⃣ The teaser loans are considered to be an aspect of sub-prime lending and banks may be exposed to the risk of defaulters in future. 2️⃣ In India, the teaser loans are mostly given to inexperienced entrepreneurs to set up manufacturing or export units. [2011-I]
questions.e: Teaser loans offer low initial interest rates that jump later. They are a concern because they can lead to sub-prime style defaults. In India, they were mostly offered for home loans, not industrial units.

questions.q: Which of the following can aid in furthering the Government's objective of inclusive growth? 1️⃣ Promoting Self-Help Groups. 2️⃣ Promoting Micro Small and Medium Enterprises. 3️⃣ Implementing the Right to Education Act. [2011-I]
questions.e: Inclusive growth requires both economic empowerment (via SHGs and MSMEs) and social empowerment (via education and health), making all three statements correct.

questions.q: Why is the Government of India disinvesting its equity in the Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)? 1️⃣ The Government intends to use the revenue earned from the disinvestment mainly to pay back the external debt. 2️⃣ The Government no longer intends to retain the management control of the CPSEs. [2011-I]
questions.e: Disinvestment is driven by fiscal constraints and the need to fund social sectors, not primarily to pay external debt. The government often retains management control even after minority disinvestment.

questions.q: Economic growth is usually coupled with: [2011-I]
questions.e: Moderate inflation is often seen as a sign of a growing economy where rising demand encourages production, leading to economic growth.

questions.q: The lowering of Bank Rate by the Reserve Bank of India leads to: [2011-I]
o: no change in the liquidity in the market
mobilization of more deposits by commercial banks
questions.e: A lower Bank Rate reduces the cost of borrowing for commercial banks from the RBI. This encourages banks to lend more, thereby increasing the money supply and liquidity in the market.

questions.q: How do District Rural Development Agencies (DRDAs) help in the reduction of rural poverty in India? 1️⃣ DRDAs act as Panchayati Raj Institutions in certain specified backward regions of the country. 2️⃣ DRDAs undertake area-specific scientific study of the causes of poverty and malnutrition and prepare detailed remedial measures. 3️⃣ DRDAs secure inter-sectoral and inter-departmental coordination and cooperation for effective implementation of anti-poverty programmes. 4️⃣ DRDAs watch over and ensure effective utilization of the funds intended for anti-poverty programmes. [2012-I]
questions.e: DRDAs are the principal district-level organs for overseeing anti-poverty programs. They focus on coordination and fund utilization but do not act as Panchayati Raj Institutions themselves.

questions.q: The Multi-dimensional Poverty Index developed by Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative with UNDP support covers which of the following? 1️⃣ Deprivation of education, health, assets and services at household level 2️⃣ Purchasing power parity at national level 3️⃣ Extent of budget deficit and GDP growth rate at national level [2012-I]
questions.e: The MPI measures poverty at the household level across dimensions of health, education, and living standards. National macro-economic indicators like GDP or budget deficits are not included in the MPI.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are among the noticeable features of the recommendations of the Thirteenth Finance Commission? 1️⃣ A design for the Goods and Services Tax, and a compensation package linked to adherence to the proposed design 2️⃣ A design for the creation of lakhs of jobs in the next ten years in consonance with India's demographic dividend 3️⃣ Devolution of a specified share of central taxes to local bodies as grants [2012-I]
questions.e: The 13th Finance Commission provided a design for GST and recommended that local bodies receive a specific percentage of the divisible pool of central taxes as grants. Job creation was not a direct recommendation of the commission.

questions.q: Consider the following specific stages of demographic transition associated with economic development: 1️⃣ Low birthrate with low death rate 2️⃣ High birthrate with high death rate 3️⃣ High birthrate with low death rate. Select the correct order of the above stages using the codes given below: [2012-I]
questions.e: Demographic transition typically begins with a high birth and death rate (pre-industrial), moves to high birth but falling death rates (developing), and ends with low birth and death rates (industrialized).

questions.q: Under which of the following circumstances may 'capital gains' arise? 1️⃣ When there is an increase in the sales of a product 2️⃣ When there is a natural increase in the value of the property owned 3️⃣ When you purchase a painting and there is a growth in its value due to increase in its popularity [2012-I]
questions.e: Capital gains refer to the increase in the value of an asset (like property or art) compared to its purchase price. An increase in the quantity of product sales is a business profit issue, not a capital gain.

questions.q: Which of the following measures would result in an increase in the money supply in the economy? 1️⃣ Purchase of government securities from the public by the Central Bank 2️⃣ Deposit of currency in commercial banks by the public 3️⃣ Borrowing by the government from the Central Bank 4️⃣ Sale of government securities to the public by the Central Bank [2012-I]
questions.e: When the Central Bank buys securities, it pumps cash into the economy. Government borrowing from the Central Bank (printing money) also increases supply. Selling securities or public deposits reduces/neutralizes circulating money.

questions.q: Which of the following would include Foreign Direct Investment in India? 1️⃣ Subsidiaries of foreign companies in India 2️⃣ Majority foreign equity holding in Indian companies 3️⃣ Companies exclusively financed by foreign companies 4️⃣ Portfolio investment [2012-I]
questions.e: FDI involves direct business interests and management control. Portfolio investment (FPI) refers to passive investment in stocks/bonds and is distinct from FDI.

questions.q: Who among the following constitute the National Development Council? 1️⃣ The Prime Minister 2️⃣ The Chairman, Finance Commission 3️⃣ Ministers of the Union Cabinet 4️⃣ Chief Ministers of the States [2013-I]
questions.e: The NDC includes the PM, Union Cabinet Ministers, all State Chief Ministers, UT administrators, and members of the Planning Commission. The Finance Commission Chairman is not a member.

questions.q: To obtain full benefits of demographic dividend, what should India do? [2013-I]
questions.e: A demographic dividend occurs when the working-age population is large. To benefit, this workforce must be productive, which requires investment in skill development and job creation.

questions.q: A rise in general level of prices may be caused by: 1️⃣ an increase in the money supply 2️⃣ a decrease in the aggregate level of output 3️⃣ an increase in the effective demand [2013-I]
questions.e: Inflation occurs when there is too much money chasing too few goods (supply decrease or demand increase), making all three factors potential causes for a price rise.

questions.q: Which one of the following is likely to be the most inflationary in its effect? [2013-I]
o: Borrowing from the public to finance a budget deficit
Creating new money to finance a budget deficit
Borrowing from banks to finance a budget deficit
questions.e: Deficit financing through the creation of new money (printing) is the most inflationary because it increases the money supply without a corresponding increase in goods or services.

questions.q: Supply of money remaining the same when there is an increase in demand for money, there will be: [2013-I]
o: a decrease in the rate of interest
an increase in the rate of interest
a fall in the level of prices
an increase in the level of income and employment
questions.e: If demand for money increases but the supply is fixed, the "price" of money—the interest rate—will rise.

questions.q: Economic growth in country X will necessarily have to occur if: [2013-I]
o: there is technical progress in the world economy
there is population growth in X
the volume of trade grows in the world economy
there is capital formation of X
questions.e: Capital formation (investment in factories, machinery, infrastructure) is a fundamental internal driver that necessarily leads to enhanced productive capacity and economic growth.

questions.q: If the interest rate is decreased in an economy, it will: [2014-I]
o: decrease the consumption expenditure in the economy
increase the tax collection of the Government
increase the total savings in the economy
increase the investment expenditure in the economy
questions.e: Lower interest rates make borrowing cheaper for businesses, encouraging them to spend on capital goods and expansion, thereby increasing investment expenditure.

questions.q: With reference to Union Budget, which of the following is/are covered under Non-Plan Expenditure? 1️⃣ Defence expenditure 2️⃣ Interest payments 3️⃣ Salaries and pensions 4️⃣ Subsidies [2014-I]
questions.e: Non-plan expenditure consists of all government spending not covered by the Five Year Plans, including core obligations like interest, defence, salaries, and subsidies.

questions.q: The sales tax you pay while purchasing a toothpaste is a: [2014-I]
o: tax imposed by the Central Government but collected by the State Government
tax imposed by the State Government but collected by the Central Government
tax imposed by the Central Government
tax imposed and collected by the State Government
questions.e: Prior to GST, sales tax (or VAT) on consumer goods like toothpaste was both imposed and collected by the State Governments.

questions.q: What does venture capital mean? [2014-I]
o: Funds provided for replacement and renovation of industries
A long-term start-up capital provided to new entrepreneurs
A short-term capital provided to industries
Funds provided to industries at times of incurring losses
questions.e: Venture capital is long-term financial capital provided to early-stage, high-potential, or high-risk start-up companies to help them grow.

questions.q: With reference to 'Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation (IOR-ARC)', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was established very recently in response to incidents of piracy and accidents of oil spills. 2️⃣ It is an alliance meant for maritime security only. [2015-I]
questions.e: IOR-ARC (now IORA) was established in 1997, not "recently." It covers six priority areas including trade, fisheries, and tourism, not just maritime security.

questions.q: With reference to inflation in India, which of the following statements is correct? [2015-I]
o: Decreased money circulation helps in controlling the inflation
The Reserve Bank of India has no role in controlling the inflation
Controlling the inflation in India is the responsibility of the Government of India only
Increased money circulation helps in controlling the inflation
questions.e: Decreasing the money supply through tight monetary policy reduces demand, which is a standard method the RBI uses to control inflation.

questions.q: There has been a persistent deficit budget year after year. Which of the following actions can be taken by the government to reduce the deficit? 1️⃣ Reducing revenue expenditure 2️⃣ Introducing new welfare schemes 3️⃣ Rationalizing subsidies 4️⃣ Expanding industries [2015-I]
questions.e: To reduce a deficit, the government must either increase income or decrease spending. Reducing revenue expenditure and rationalizing subsidies decrease spending; new welfare schemes or expanding state industries would increase it.

questions.q: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane is approved by the: [2015-I]
o: Directorate of Marketing and Inspection, Ministry of Agriculture
Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
questions.e: While the CACP recommends the price, the final approval for the FRP of sugarcane rests with the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).

questions.q: 'Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana' has been launched for: [2015-I]
o: providing housing loan to poor people at cheaper interest rates
promoting women's Self-Help Groups in backward areas
providing financial help to the marginalized communities
promoting financial inclusion in the country
questions.e: PMJDY is a national mission for financial inclusion, ensuring that every household has access to banking services, credit, and insurance.

questions.q: With reference to the Fourteenth Finance Commission, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It has increased the share of States in the central divisible pool from 32 percent to 42 percent. 2️⃣ It has made recommendations concerning sector-specific grants. [2015-I]
questions.e: The 14th Finance Commission significantly increased the states' share of the divisible pool to 42%. However, it moved away from sector-specific grants to give states more autonomy over their spending.

questions.q: Convertibility of rupee implies: [2015-I]
o: allowing the value of rupee to be fixed by market forces
freely permitting the conversion of rupee to other currencies and vice versa
being able to convert rupee notes into gold
developing an international market for currencies in India
questions.e: Currency convertibility is the ease with which a country's currency can be exchanged for gold or other foreign currencies in the open market.

questions.q: The Government of India has established NITI Aayog to replace the: [2015-I]
questions.e: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on January 1, 2015, replacing the Planning Commission to serve as a policy think tank.

questions.q: With reference to 'Financial Stability and Development Council', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an organ of NITI Aayog. 2️⃣ It is headed by the Union Finance Minister. 3️⃣ It monitors macroprudential supervision of the economy. [2016-I]
questions.e: The FSDC is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Finance, not NITI Aayog. It is chaired by the Finance Minister and focuses on financial stability and inter-regulatory coordination.

questions.q: Regarding 'Atal Pension Yojana', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is a minimum guaranteed pension scheme mainly targeted at unorganized sector workers. 2️⃣ Only one member of a family can join the scheme. 3️⃣ Same amount of pension is guaranteed for the spouse for life after subscriber's death. [2016-I]
questions.e: APY is for the unorganized sector. There is no "one member per family" restriction. If the subscriber dies, the spouse receives the same pension amount for life.

questions.q: With reference to 'Stand up India scheme', which of the following statement is/are correct? 1️⃣ Its purpose is to promote entrepreneurship among SC/ST and women entrepreneurs. 2️⃣ It provides for refinance through SIDBI. [2016-I]
questions.e: Stand Up India promotes entrepreneurship by providing bank loans to SC/ST and women. It includes a refinance window of 10,000 crore through SIDBI.

questions.q: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana is aimed at: [2016-I]
o: providing pensions to old and destitute persons
providing loans to poor farmers for cultivating particular crops
funding the voluntary organizations involved in the promotion of skill development and employment generation
bringing the small entrepreneurs into formal financial system
questions.e: MUDRA provides funding to non-corporate, small business sectors to help them access credit from the formal financial system.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a purpose of 'UDAY', a scheme of the Government? [2016-I]
o: Providing electricity to every household in the country by 2018
Replacing the coal-based power plants with natural gas, nuclear, solar, wind and tidal power plants over a period of time
Providing technical and financial assistance to start-up entrepreneurs in the field of renewable sources of energy
Providing for financial turnaround and revival of power distribution companies
questions.e: Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY) was launched to solve the financial distress of power distribution companies (DISCOMs) through debt restructuring and efficiency improvements.

questions.q: What is/are the purpose/purposes of 'District Mineral Foundations in India? 1️⃣ Promoting mineral exploration activities in mineral-rich districts 2️⃣ Protecting the interests of the persons affected by mining operations 3️⃣ Authorizing State Governments to issue licences for mineral exploration [2016-I]
questions.e: DMFs are non-profit trusts set up in mining-affected districts to work for the benefit of the people and areas affected by mining. They do not issue licenses or promote exploration.

questions.q: 'SWAYAM', an initiative of the Government of India, aims at: [2016-I]
o: promoting the education and health of adolescent girls
promoting the Self Help Groups in rural areas
providing affordable and quality education to the citizens for free
providing financial and technical assistance to young start-up entrepreneurs
questions.e: SWAYAM provides online courses from top professors at IITs and IIMs to all citizens for free to ensure quality education reaches everyone.

questions.q: Regarding DigiLocker, sometimes seen in the news, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is a digital locker system offered by the Government under Digital India Programme. 2️⃣ It allows you to access your e-documents irrespective of your physical location. [2016-I]
questions.e: DigiLocker provides citizens with a secure cloud-based platform for storage, sharing, and verification of documents, accessible anywhere via the internet.

questions.q: 'Mission Indradhanush' launched by the Government of India pertains to: [2016-I]
o: immunization of children and pregnant women
construction of smart cities across the country
India's own search for the Earth-like planets in outer space
questions.e: Mission Indradhanush aims to achieve full immunization coverage for all children under two and pregnant women by 2020.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) helps in promoting the financial inclusion in the country. 2️⃣ NPCI has launched RuPay, a card payment scheme. [2017-I]
questions.e: NPCI is a non-profit company that provides payment infrastructure like RuPay and UPI, which are essential tools for expanding financial inclusion.

questions.q: Which of the following is a most likely consequence of implementing the 'Unified Payments Interface (UPI)'? [2017-I]
o: Mobile wallets will not be necessary for online payments.
Direct transfer of subsidies to poor people will become very effective.
Digital currency will totally replace the physical currency in about two decades.
questions.e: Because UPI allows direct bank-to-bank transfers via mobile apps, users do not need to load money into a separate mobile wallet to make online payments.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)? 1️⃣ It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates. 2️⃣ It is a 12-member body including the Governor of RBI and is reconstituted every year. 3️⃣ It functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister. [2017-I]
questions.e: The MPC has 6 members (not 12) and is chaired by the Governor of the RBI (not the Finance Minister). Its primary role is to set the benchmark interest rate (repo rate).

questions.q: What is the purpose of setting up of Small Finance Banks (SFBs) in India? 1️⃣ To supply credit to small business units 2️⃣ To supply credit to small and marginal farmers 3️⃣ To encourage young entrepreneurs to set up business particularly in rural areas. [2017-I]
questions.e: According to RBI guidelines, the specific objectives of SFBs are to provide credit to small business units and small/marginal farmers to further financial inclusion.

questions.q: Who among the following can join the National Pension System (NPS)? [2017-I]
o: All Central Government employees including those of Armed Forces joining the services on or after 1st April, 2004
All State Government employees joining the services after the date of notification by the respective State Governments
Persons of age from 21 to 55 only
questions.e: NPS is open to most citizens (including NRIs) between 18-65. It is mandatory for state government employees (depending on state notification) and central employees except for the armed forces.

questions.q: What is/are the most likely advantages of implementing 'Goods and Services Tax (GST)'? 1️⃣ It will replace multiple taxes collected by multiple authorities and will thus create a single market in India. 2️⃣ It will drastically reduce the 'Current Account Deficit' of India and will enable it to increase its foreign exchange reserves. 3️⃣ It will enormously increase the growth and size of economy of India and will enable it to overtake China in the near future. [2017-I]
questions.e: GST's primary benefit is consolidating taxes into a single market. Claims about "drastic" CAD reduction or "enormous" growth that overtakes China are considered extreme and unlikely based on economic projections.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (PBPT Act)', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A property transaction is not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware of the transaction. 2️⃣ Properties held benami are liable for confiscation by the Government. 3️⃣ The Act provides for three authorities for investigations but does not provide for any appellate mechanism. [2017-I]
questions.e: The government has the power to confiscate benami properties. The Act does provide for an appellate mechanism (Appellate Tribunal), and awareness of the owner is not a sole criteria for exemption.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Tax revenue as a per cent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade. 2️⃣ Fiscal deficit as a per cent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade. [2017-I]
questions.e: Economic data shows that both tax revenue and fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP have fluctuated over the last decade rather than showing a "steady" increase.

questions.q: What is the aim of the programme 'Unnat Bharat Abhiyan'? [2017-I]
o: Developing human capital by allocating special funds for health care and education of rural and urban poor, and organizing skill development programmes and vocational training for them.
Connecting institutions of higher education with local communities to address development challenges through appropriate technologies.
Strengthening India's scientific research institutions in order to make India a scientific and technological power.
Achieving 100% literacy by promoting collaboration between voluntary organizations and government's education system and local communities.
questions.e: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan aims to link higher education institutions with rural communities to help solve development issues through the application of technology and knowledge.

questions.q: With reference to 'National Investment and Infrastructure Fund', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is an organ of NITI Aayog. 2️⃣ It has a corpus of 4,00,000 crore at present. [2017-I]
questions.e: NIIF is under the Department of Economic Affairs, not NITI Aayog. Its original planned corpus was 40,000 crore, making the 4 lakh crore figure incorrect.

questions.q: Which of the following are the objectives of 'National Nutrition Mission'? 1️⃣ To create awareness relating to malnutrition among pregnant women and lactating mothers. 2️⃣ To reduce the incidence of anemia among young children, adolescent girls and women. 3️⃣ To promote the consumption of millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice. 4️⃣ To promote the consumption of poultry eggs. [2017-I]
questions.e: The mission focuses on awareness and reducing anemia. While it may indirectly influence consumption, promoting specific foods like millets or eggs is not an explicitly stated core objective.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'Vidyanjali Yojana'? 1️⃣ To enable the famous foreign educational institutions to open their campuses in India. 2️⃣ To increase the quality of education provided in government schools by taking help from the private sector and the community. 3️⃣ To encourage voluntary monetary contributions from private individuals and organizations so as to improve the infrastructure facilities for primary and secondary schools. [2017-I]
questions.e: Vidyanjali encourages community and private sector volunteering in government schools. It focuses on human service rather than infrastructure funding for secondary schools.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Reserve Bank of India manages and services Government of India Securities but not any State Government Securities. 2️⃣ Treasury bills are issued by the Government of India and there are no treasury bills issued by the State Governments. 3️⃣ Treasury bills are issued at a discount from the par value. [2018-I]
questions.e: RBI manages debt for both Union and State governments. States do not issue Treasury bills; they are exclusively issued by the Central Government at a discount to their face value.

questions.q: If a commodity is provided free to the public by the Government, then: [2018-I]
o: the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the products to the Government.
the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the tax-paying public.
questions.e: Providing a free service still requires resources that could have been used elsewhere. This opportunity cost is borne by the public who funds the government through taxes.

questions.q: Increase in absolute and per capita real GNP do not connote a higher level of economic development, if: [2018-I]
o: industrial output fails to keep pace with agricultural output.
agricultural output fails to keep pace with industrial output.
questions.e: Economic development is broader than growth; it includes improvements in the quality of life. If growth occurs alongside rising poverty and unemployment, it is not considered true development.

questions.q: Atal innovation mission is set up under the: [2019-I]
o: Ministry of skill development and entrepreneurship
questions.e: The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) is a flagship initiative housed within NITI Aayog to promote innovation and entrepreneurship.

questions.q: In a given year in India, official poverty lines are higher in some states than in other because: [2019-I]
o: Gross state product varies from state to state
Quality of public distribution varies from state to state
Price levels vary from state to state
Poverty rates vary from state to state
questions.e: Poverty lines are updated based on Consumer Price Indices (CPIAL for rural, CPIIW for urban), which reflect state-specific price levels for essential goods.

questions.q: With reference to India's Five Year Plans, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ From the Second Five-Year Plan, there was a determined thrust towards substitution of basic and capital good industries. 2️⃣ The Fourth Five-Year Plan adopted the objective of correcting the earlier trend of increased concentration of wealth and economic power. 3️⃣ In the Fifth Five-Year Plan, for the first time, the financial sector was included as an integral part of the Plan. [2019-I]
questions.e: The Second Plan pushed heavy industry, and the Fourth Plan aimed at wealth redistribution. The Fifth Plan focused on poverty removal and self-reliance, not specifically the integration of the financial sector.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017? 1️⃣ Pregnant women are entitled for three months pre-delivery and three months post-delivery paid leave 2️⃣ Enterprises with creches must allow the mother minimum six creche visits daily 3️⃣ Women with two children get reduced entitlements. [2019-I]
questions.e: Women with two or more children receive 12 weeks of leave, while those with fewer receive 26 weeks. The Act mandates four creche visits per day, not six.

questions.q: Considering the following statements: 1️⃣ Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) exchange rates are calculated by the prices of the same basket of goods and services in different countries. 2️⃣ In terms of PPP dollars, India is the sixth largest economy in the world. [2019-I]
questions.e: PPP compares purchasing power across countries using a standard basket of goods. In terms of PPP, India is the third-largest economy, not sixth.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not the most likely measure the Government/RBI takes to stop the slide of Indian rupee? [2019-I]
o: Easing conditions relating to external commercial borrowing
Curbing imports of non-essential goods and promoting exports
Encouraging indian borrowers to issue rupee denominated Masala bonds
questions.e: Expansionary policy increases the supply of rupees, which would further weaken the currency. To support the rupee, a central bank usually tightens money supply.

questions.q: The money multiplier in an economy increases with which one of the following? [2019-I]
o: Increase in the population of the country
Increase in the cash reserve ratio
Increase in the banking habit of the population
questions.e: As more people use banks (banking habit), more money is cycled through the lending process, which increases the money multiplier effect.

questions.q: If another global financial crisis happens in the near future, which of the following actions/policies are most likely to give some immunity to India? 1️⃣ Not depending on short-term foreign borrowings 2️⃣ Opening up to more foreign banks 3️⃣ Maintaining full capital account convertibility [2020-I]
questions.e: Short-term foreign debt is volatile during crises. Full capital convertibility or excessive foreign bank presence could allow global financial contagion to spread more easily to India.

questions.q: If you withdraw Rs. 1,00,000 in cash from your Demand Deposit Account at your bank, the immediate effect on aggregate money supply in the economy will be: [2020-I]
o: to increase it by more than 1,00,000
questions.e: M3 (aggregate money supply) includes both currency with the public and deposits. Withdrawing cash simply moves the money from "deposits" to "currency with public," leaving the total M3 unchanged.

questions.q: Along with the Budget, the Finance Minister also places other documents before the Parliament which include 'The Macro Economic Framework Statement'. The aforesaid document is presented because this is mandated by: [2020-I]
o: Provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
Article 112 and Article 110(1) of the Constitution of India
Article 113 of the Constitution of India
questions.e: The FRBM Act, 2003 requires the government to present the Macro-Economic Framework Statement to ensure transparency in fiscal and economic management.

questions.q: Under the Kisan Credit Card scheme, short-term credit support is given to farmers for which of the following purposes? 1️⃣ Working capital for maintenance of farm assets 2️⃣ Purchase of combine harvesters, tractors and mini trucks 3️⃣ Consumption requirements of farm households 4️⃣ Post-harvest expenses 5️⃣ Construction of family house and setting up of village cold storage facility [2020-I]
questions.e: KCC provides short-term credit for crop cultivation, maintenance, post-harvest, and household consumption. Big machinery or house construction requires long-term loans, not the short-term credit provided by KCC.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The weightage of food in Consumer Price Index (CPI) is higher than that in Wholesale Price Index (WPI). 2️⃣ The WPI does not capture changes in the prices of services, which CPI does. 3️⃣ Reserve Bank of India has now adopted WPI as its key measure of inflation and to decide on changing the key policy rates. [2020-I]
questions.e: Food has a higher weight in CPI as it tracks consumer spending. WPI only covers goods, while CPI includes services. Since 2014, the RBI uses CPI as its primary inflation target.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian economy after the 1991 economic liberalization, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Worker productivity per worker (at 2004-05 prices) increased in urban areas while it decreased in rural areas. 2️⃣ The percentage share of rural areas in the workforce steadily increased. 3️⃣ In rural areas, the growth in the non-farm economy increased. 4️⃣ The growth rate in rural employment decreased. [2020-I]
questions.e: Post-1991, the workforce shifted from agriculture to non-farm sectors. This led to a decrease in the rural employment growth rate while increasing the non-farm economy in rural areas.

questions.q: In India, under cyber insurance for individuals, which of the following benefits are generally covered, in addition to payment for the loss of funds and other benefits? 1️⃣ Cost of restoration of the computer system in case of malware disrupting access to one's computer 2️⃣ Cost of a new computer if some miscreant wilfully damages it, if proved so 3️⃣ Cost of hiring a specialized consultant to minimize the loss in case of cyber extortion 4️⃣ Cost of defence in the Court of Law if any third party files a suit [2020-I]
questions.e: Cyber insurance covers digital risks like malware, extortion, and legal defense against third-party suits. Physical damage to hardware by a neighbor or miscreant is a property insurance issue, not cyber insurance.
